newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen higher at start.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen higher at start.

text.p: Wall Street stocks, underpinned by a steady bond market, are expected to move higher at the start of trading Wednesday, following through on the second largest advance in Dow history.
The Dow industrials rallied 173 points on Tuesday to close at 6834, driven by short covering and program trading which made for a mixed performance in the broad market.
Trading will unfold in anticipation of the first quarter earnings report due from International Business Machines Corp after the market close today.
Despite the move in the Dow, analysts like Prudential Securities' Larry Wachtel remained cautious, saying that the rally was once again concentrated in blue chips.

"Yesterday was a decent day for the broad market and a great day for the Dow," he said. "It was a thin rally. This is the fifth time this year that the Dow has risen over a hundred points. We take these swings in our stride.

"But you have to wonder when we see a move like that on a day bereft of any fundamental drama. There was no news. Suddenly there were buy programs. Everything that happens in the Dow comes from Chicago."
He said that bonds would again lead stocks today and that investors will keep an eye on today's U.S. Treasury auction of $12.5 billion in five year notes.
Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said he expected the move to continue today.

"A spectacular move like this doesn't stop on a dime. It was concentrated in a handful of stocks again, but I would imagine we continue today as earnings are okay this morning and there is no economic data," he said.
According to First Call, IBM is expected to report earnings per share of $2.28 per share versus $2.21 a year ago.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average finished at 18,735.47 after gaining 191.02 points, or 1.03 percent.
In London, the FTSE 100 Index was up 48.4 at 4394.5.

U.S. stocks traded in London were mostly holding firm on Wednesday after Tuesday's Wall Street surge. IBM was down 1/4 at 139-1/4. Shares of Eli Lilly and Co were quoted up 1/4 at 85-1/4, Pfizer Inc was up 1/8 at 92 and Warner-Lambert was up 3/8 at 99. Philip Morris Cos Inc was up 1/4 at 42-1/4. Novell Inc was down 1/4 at 8-3/4. Intel Corp was quoted up 3/8 at 29-1/4.
WMX Technologies Inc was up 3/8 at 29-1/4.
The dollar drifted lower against the yen in Tokyo and was steady in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries were unchanged to slightly higher, with the long bond up 1/32 to yield 7.04 percent.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street writes that investors are less elated by the $10.2 billion merger pact between Morgan Stanley Group Inc and Dean Witter Discover & Co than they were after the plan was unveiled on February 5. Both stocks have underperformed indexes of brokerage industry and financial industry stocks.
The New York Times Market Place writes that investors tolerant of high risk should prepare for a series of crucial events as negotiations involving the tobacco industry unfold.
They range from near-term wild cards dealt by court decisions to some quite probable bad hands at the negotiating table.
